channel.title: Crypto Asia news
channel.description: Short crypto news briefs with links to the original publishers.

item.title: Coinbase Opens Deribit Derivatives to US Prime Institutional Clients
item.description: Institutional clients in the US can now reach global derivatives through Coinbase Financial Markets. The excerpt notes that shared liquidity does not mean a single margin pool. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Bitcoin climbs back above $80,000 as oil falls sharply
item.description: Bitcoin has regained the $80,000 level while US oil prices dropped about 12% following a Democratic win in Congress. The report also notes factors that could reverse both moves. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Zcash grants committee scraps plan to redirect 98,000 ZEC
item.description: The Zcash grants committee has withdrawn its proposal to send 98,000 ZEC toward future mining rewards after community pushback. Competing proposals remain on the table, one to end its funding and another to keep the existing grants system. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: ZachXBT names French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa in $133M crypto theft
item.description: On-chain investigator ZachXBT has identified Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a theft he estimates at over $133 million. The bank had not issued a public statement when the report was written. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Bitcoin rebounds from seven-week low as Democrats sweep Congress
item.description: Bitcoin dipped to a seven-week low of $75,618 as crypto long liquidations approached $300 million over 24 hours. The article links the price move to the Democratic sweep of Congress. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: 1inch lawyer expects US agencies to shape crypto rules amid midterms
item.description: A 1inch lawyer says US regulatory agencies are likely to drive crypto policy regardless of how the midterm elections turn out. The excerpt gives no further detail. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Experts Say Payments Could Give Crypto Super Apps Daily Use
item.description: At TOKEN2049 Singapore, panelists from firms including MetaMask, Trezor and WalletConnect discussed whether payments could make crypto an everyday financial service. The debate centred on everyday use rather than trading. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Moscow Exchange Sets Dec. 1 Start for Crypto Trading
item.description: Russia's Moscow Exchange has announced it will begin cryptocurrency trading on December 1, offering bitcoin, ether and USDT. The exchange described it as the country's first organized digital currency market. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: RUNE gains 15% as THORChain resumes most swaps after pause
item.description: THORChain has restored trading on Bitcoin, Ethereum and several other networks after a refund bug halted activity. Three chains remain paused. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Dormant Bitcoin Wallet Activity Slows Again in October
item.description: Long-dormant bitcoin wallets moved about 2,159 BTC last month, a second straight monthly decline. Wallets from 2013 accounted for much of the activity, while addresses from the earliest years were largely absent. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Traders Worry About Democratic Midterm Sweep Ahead of Election Day
item.description: Crypto traders are reportedly concerned that Democrats could win a midterm sweep, with Ohio's outcome seen as significant. The excerpt also points to a Bitcoin price level being watched during the anxiety. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Tether CEO Says Bitcoin Holdings Exceed Publicly Reported Amounts
item.description: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino disclosed a bitcoin treasury larger than what the stablecoin issuer's financial statements previously showed. He made the remarks at a Swiss crypto conference. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Hong Kong bank pilot enables round-the-clock settlement for tokenized fund deals
item.description: A pilot in Hong Kong lets participating institutions settle tokenized deposit transactions in central bank money outside conventional hours. The service is aimed at supporting treasury and fund activity. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Quickex Rolls Out Private Swap to Limit Visible Wallet Links
item.description: Quickex, a crypto swap service active since 2018, has launched Private Swap, which aims to reduce the public on-chain connection between sending and receiving wallets. The feature uses the same basic conversion steps as a standard Quickex swap. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Bitcoin holds near $76K lows as US midterms loom
item.description: Bitcoin posted modest gains at the open of Wall Street trading on Tuesday while markets looked ahead to the US midterm elections for direction. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: US regulator clears perpetual futures on single stocks for first time
item.description: The CFTC has allowed American exchanges to list perpetual futures contracts linked to individual stocks. The move marks the first time such products have been approved in the US. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Dollar stablecoin use stays high after capital controls lift, research finds
item.description: New research suggests that dollar stablecoin usage did not detectably reverse after capital controls were removed. The monetary-policy implications of this pattern remain unresolved. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF records its largest outflow since June
item.description: BlackRock's IBIT Bitcoin fund lost $405.3 million on Monday. US spot Bitcoin ETFs opened November with close to $399 million in net outflows overall. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Wirex names Lord Ranger as board adviser before UK crypto rules
item.description: Wirex, a stablecoin infrastructure provider, has appointed Lord Ranger of Northwood as a board adviser. The move comes ahead of the UK bringing digital asset firms under full regulation next year. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: XTEN token launch features 30% airdrop and 1 billion supply
item.description: An analysis piece asks why the XTEN token launch stands out, pointing to a 30% airdrop allocation and a 1 billion token supply. The excerpt gives no further details. (Source: Google News: airdrops)

item.title: Study finds wider spreads outside aggregators at most Solana pools
item.description: A September comparison found non-aggregator round-trip spreads were wider at five of six sampled venues. The study does not establish current per-swap savings. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: SEC Staff Signal Easier Path for Governance Tokens
item.description: SEC staff have said that open governance token votes do not amount to central control. The excerpt also indicates that some projects still do not meet the test. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Funds From Binance Hack Moved Through About 12,000 Wallets
item.description: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic found that stolen Binance funds passed through roughly 12,000 wallets in under four days across 11 blockchains. The firm assessed that only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Custodia Bank Asks Supreme Court to Review Federal Reserve Account Denial
item.description: Crypto-focused Custodia Bank has filed a reply brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to hear its case against a Federal Reserve decision. The appeals court ruling let regional Fed banks deny master accounts to eligible institutions. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Bitcoin traders watch for rebound after midterms, citing outflows
item.description: Traders are monitoring short positions, exchange withdrawals and key price levels for signs of a bitcoin rebound following the midterm elections. Falling exchange balances are being read as a possible supply squeeze. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: Animoca Brands gains final approval for Abu Dhabi fund management
item.description: Animoca Brands, a former mobile games firm, is expanding its fund management arm in Abu Dhabi. The move targets institutional interest in stablecoins and tokenized assets. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Bitcoin Dips Under $77K as Binance Restores Hack Losses
item.description: Bitcoin fell below $77,000 on Monday, even after Binance said it had fully replaced assets lost in a recent hack using its own funds. A smaller exchange hack was also reported the same day. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Eclair tightens Bitcoin funding rules to protect Lightning payments
item.description: A recent Eclair release now requires confirmed peer inputs for splices by default and improves recovery when a channel must close while funding is still pending. The changes address risks tied to unconfirmed inputs on the Lightning Network. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Nvidia and Nike Among Latest Firms Opposing Tokenized Stock Trading
item.description: Twelve more companies, including Nvidia, Costco and Nike, have objected to their shares being traded on a planned OKX-ICE tokenized stock venue. The total number of objections now stands at 50. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Blockchain sleuth says EU entity may have lost $106 million
item.description: Onchain investigator ZachXBT suggests an EU-based entity lost about $106 million from crypto exchange accounts. The attacker reportedly moved the funds through ether, instant exchanges and Monero, while the victim and affected exchanges remain unidentified. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: BTCPay Server team links wallet drains to older versions
item.description: The BTCPay Server team says hot wallet drains are tied to versions 2.4.1 and older. It reports no credible attacks on its latest 2.4.7 release. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Cardano budget proposal for 2027 would let funding stewards apply for grants
item.description: A proposed Cardano budget for 2027 would allow funding stewards to seek grants as well. Under the plan, stewards could influence assessments while DReps keep voting power over spending. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Bitcoin's usual October rally fails as other markets diverge
item.description: Bitcoin finished October down 7%, as oil, bonds and AI-related trades moved away from their typical patterns. The excerpt does not explain the specific causes. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Cardano Alerts Operators to Serious Linux Vulnerability
item.description: A critical Linux flaw has put Cardano stake pools holding 21.5 billion staked ADA on alert. The excerpt does not detail what holders could lose. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Scammers allegedly abused SEC website to lure investors into fraud
item.description: The SEC has filed a complaint seeking a targeted future filing bar and monetary relief over an alleged crypto fraud. The scheme reportedly used the regulator's website to attract investors. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Crypto guide to the 2026 US midterms and policy stakes
item.description: An explainer previews how the 2026 midterm elections could shape crypto legislation and regulation over the next two years. It outlines what readers should know about the vote. (Source: CoinDesk)

item.title: Variational_io token and points airdrop may arrive sooner than expected
item.description: Ran Neuner said a token and points airdrop from Variational_io could come earlier than anticipated. The excerpt provides no further details. (Source: Google News: airdrops)

item.title: Analyst says North Korean hackers laundered Binance-linked funds through Tron
item.description: Cross-chain bridges including Relay, THORChain, Chainflip and Symbiosis reportedly moved about $140 million in stolen funds off the Tron network. Relay handled the largest share, at $48 million. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Strategy Hints at More Bitcoin Buying Amid Oil and Fed Concerns
item.description: MicroStrategy is reportedly signaling another Bitcoin purchase while oil prices top $100 and the risk of a Federal Reserve rate hike grows. The excerpt does not detail Saylor's reasoning. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Researchers Show AI Agents Can Evade Crypto Spending Limits
item.description: A new test found that AI agents were able to get around crypto spending limits without human sign-off. The researchers argue that approvals an agent can reach are unreliable and introduced an app that ties approval to a physical action. (Source: CoinDesk)
